name: ClickHouse Loom
description: Self-hosted MCP server for shared agent memory, cited document retrieval and code intelligence, with local embedding and LLM options.
compatibility: LLM jobs on Ollama or llama.cpp llama-server using the OpenAI chat-completions format.
limitations: Preview evidence is pinned to v1.3.0-rc.1; final 1.3.0 is not published. This entry has not qualified a local-model runtime or any OS or hardware target.

Self-hosted deployment needs Docker containers or a Kubernetes cluster. The documented Windows route needs WSL 2; platform and hardware tags are omitted because physical target tests are not established for this entry.

The released-image configuration carries a CPU embedder and uses a development placeholder LLM. A source checkout defaults to fake embedding and LLM providers; configure real providers for meaningful semantic search, extraction and generated answers.

Local LLM jobs require a separately installed Ollama or llama.cpp server and model. Model context, memory and latency requirements vary; local-model quality and hardware suitability are unmeasured here.

Local providers do not guarantee offline operation or private client behavior. Hosted provider overrides, independently configured coding clients and optional trace exports can send processed data elsewhere.

sources.note: Shared memory, document search, code intelligence, self-hosted deployment and coding-agent integrations.
Docker and source-build setup, Python and Compose prerequisites, bundled-image local embeddings versus checkout fake defaults, and documented WSL 2 requirements; these are not physical target tests.
Local Ollama and llama.cpp configuration, model/context and extraction limits, independent client providers and per-job hosted overrides; no local-model benchmark is claimed.
Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint and documented Claude Code and Codex plugins.
Document retrieval with source citations; the calling agent or model writes the answer.
Self-hosted Kubernetes deployment with the Helm chart.
Default local telemetry storage and optional export to a configured OTLP endpoint.
Optional trace export to a separately configured service.
